input.quote: Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation, and the media on which the Software is distributed will be free from defects in materials and workmanship under normal use, for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period").
input.rationale: Section 7.3 gives a real conformance-to-Documentation warranty for the Software and the MarketSite.net Service, and Section 7.4 adds a no-malicious-code warranty; Section 7.9's disclaimer is limited to implied warranties and does not swallow it. The remedies (commercially reasonable correction, free replacement, and a refund of all prepaid fees where the breach cannot be corrected) satisfy the fallback repair/replacement and refund elements, and the 60-day period already exceeds the 30-day services floor. However, the Warranty Period is only sixty days from the Effective Date and is further capped at December 31, 1999, which falls short of the 90-day software conformance floor at the fallback level — a material term. Our redline is the shortest change: extend the single Warranty Period to ninety days and delete the outside date that would otherwise truncate it (the December 31, 1999 cap must go, or the extension would be contradicted). We have not sought the preferred 12-month software period or added workmanlike/compliance-with-laws warranties.

proposal.summary: Extend the Warranty Period to 90 days and drop the December 31, 1999 outside date
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our warranty position requires software to be warranted to conform to its Documentation for at least 90 days, so we have extended the Warranty Period from sixty to ninety days and removed the December 31, 1999 cut-off that would otherwise truncate it. The existing correction/replacement and refund remedies are unchanged.
